findings.title: Nonuniqueness does not rule out a canonical construction relative to the supplied splitting
findings.description: The initial splitting s is part of the task data. Even with nonzero Hom_G(C,A), a canonical selection relative to that data may exist: for trivial G, s itself; with explicit invertibility of |G|, averaging s. The shear argument only rules out a choice-independent selection from an unpointed exact sequence under all sequence isomorphisms.
findings.correction: Separate unsupported uniqueness from an unsupported claim of a preferred splitting determined by the short exact sequence alone and independent of the initial splitting. Accept natural constructions relative to explicitly supplied extra data.
findings.witness: For G trivial, 0->k->k^2->k->0 has a nonzero k-dimensional difference space, yet its supplied splitting is already equivariant and naturally specified in the category of sequences with that chosen splitting.
findings.resolved_by: Original author correction integrated by parent and independently reread from the main repository
findings.verification: Reference lines 68 and 98-118 distinguish E from (E,s), the scope of shear automorphisms, transport of the averaging map, and its dependence on invariant changes of s. All new formulas are correct. The rubric now separates unsupported uniqueness from a universal s-independent natural choice, and explicitly accepts constructions canonical relative to s.
